description: Timer for a performance: it counts a clock into four bars of your own lengths and times the set in minutes, with a shaped envelope at the start of each bar and at each minute and five-minute mark

params.text: Puts the bar count, the note counts and the elapsed time back to zero, and fires both of the minute-based outputs at once
Starts and stops the timer on each press
Sets what share of each span the envelope fills, 1% to 99%: for a bar output that is a share of the bar, for the two minute-based outputs a share of five minutes and of one minute
Chooses the shape every output takes, stepping through a slow rise to a vertical drop, a triangle, a vertical jump to a slow fall, a half sine and a flat pulse
Sets how many clocks the first bar lasts, 1 to 16
Sets how many clocks the second bar lasts, 1 to 16
Sets how many clocks the third bar lasts, 1 to 16
Sets how many clocks the fourth bar lasts, 1 to 16

inputs.text: Each rising edge above 1V is counted as one sixteenth note; the four bar lengths are counted in these, and every fourth edge flashes the lamp
A rising edge above 1V puts the counters back to zero and fires both of the minute-based outputs
A rising edge above 1V starts the timer if it is stopped and stops it if it is running

outputs.text: An envelope fired at each reset and then every five minutes until thirty minutes have passed, lasting the share of five minutes set by the percentage knob
An envelope fired at each reset and then every minute until fifteen minutes have passed, lasting the share of one minute set by the percentage knob
An envelope fired when the cycle enters the first bar, lasting the share of that bar set by the percentage knob
An envelope fired when the cycle enters the second bar, lasting the share of that bar set by the percentage knob
An envelope fired when the cycle enters the third bar, lasting the share of that bar set by the percentage knob
An envelope fired when the cycle enters the fourth bar, lasting the share of that bar set by the percentage knob

notes: nothing counts until the start button is pressed or a rising edge reaches the start jack. All six outputs rest at 0V until then.
the minutes are taken from the computer's own clock rather than from the clock jack, so they do not follow the tempo. Only the bars are counted in clocks.
the five-minute output stops firing after thirty minutes and the one-minute output after fifteen; only a reset brings them back.
